answer.rationale: The line is running at 94% committed volume with zero buffer, so any delivery disruption is high-stakes right now. Switching primary supply to an unproven low-cost vendor (memory_c2) would meet the 18% cost mandate on paper, but that memory only attests to price, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy — it says nothing about delivery reliability under sustained full-volume production, which is the actual risk that matters given the zero-buffer condition. Memory_c1 shows the incumbent has already delivered two cycles of stable, uninterrupted integration, and memory_c4 shows that renegotiation at renewal, backed by market-rate benchmarking, previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without touching the vendor relationship. Given the 14-day expiry forces action this cycle, negotiating renewal terms with the incumbent using competitive benchmarks is the path most likely to satisfy the cost mandate while not introducing new delivery risk. I want to verify memory_c4's archived record to confirm how large the recovered margin actually was and under what leverage conditions, since 'real margin' is vague and I need to judge whether negotiation alone can plausibly close enough of the gap toward the 18% target before treating this as sufficient, versus needing to revisit switching or second-sourcing next cycle. Full switch to the low-cost vendor is deferred as unverified at this capacity/risk level, not ruled out.
